title: How does an AI agent use a paid tool through MCP?
abstract: Sourced guide to how does an AI agent use a paid tool through MCP. Includes evidence limits.
body:
According to ResearchAgent documentation, an AI agent uses the MCP ask_expert tool to request research with a budget; deterministic policy selects and pays for evidence within the admitted allowance. [2] [3] [4]

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, lets a server describe tools with names and input schemas so an agent client can discover and invoke them. A tool call is a request to the server, not proof of a payment or delivery. MCP itself does not supply a wallet, establish a writer’s honesty or grant unrestricted authority over the caller’s money. [1]

The ResearchAgent client asks a question, receives a run identifier and can read progress and the completed answer. The server searches writers and evaluates whether paid evidence fills a gap. Purchases remain subject to source, per-call and wallet daily limits. MCP cap arguments cannot raise operator-owned authority, and a repeated intent key cannot authorize a second charge for the same request. [2] [3] [4]

Author interpretation: configure the allowance before handing the tool to an agent, then inspect citations and receipts after completion. The standard research tool gives the model a way to ask; it does not expose a free-form sign-anything operation. A useful integration should also let the client observe pending work, read wallet status and distinguish fixture demonstrations from live provider execution. Sources accessed 10 November 2026. [3] [4]
